snip.t: If unchecked: Septic cascade → Systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) → Hypotension, organ dysfunction → Septic shock.
Systemic inflammatory response – cytokines (IL‑8, TNF‑α) and acute‑phase reactants: Persistent systemic inflammation contributes to weight loss, anemia and, in severe cases, secondary amyloidosis.
Systemic inflammatory response (release of cytokines, inflammatory mediators)
| Full blood count | Assesses systemic inflammatory response | Normocytic anemia, marked neutrophil leukocytosis |
Pyrogen release (TNF-alpha, IL-1, IL-6) from infected macrophages causing systemic inflammatory response and relative bradycardia

Examination – General: *Temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, mental status, skin colour, jaundice, lymphadenopathy, rash, petechiae?* — Fever, tachycardia, hypotension = systemic inflammatory response; rash/petechiae may indicate meningococcemia or drug reaction.
Systemic inflammatory response (SIRS) criteria: Fever/hypothermia, tachycardia, tachypnoea, leukocytosis/leukopenia.
Sepsis and Septic Shock: Severe infections can trigger a systemic inflammatory response.
